newsitem.title: UK: Med oil products mostly weaker as futures fall.
newsitem.headline: Med oil products mostly weaker as futures fall.

text.p: Mediterranean oil products were mostly weaker on Friday, traders said.

Gasoline was still tight. Arbitrage opportunities from northwest Europe to the U.S. were considered closed and dealers said they expect material in northwest Europe to move to the Med. But no business was seen on this basis.
Naphtha was steady to weaker in line with falling crude futures. An industry function in Scandinavia hampered trade.
Gas oil was flat in a continuing slack market, traders said.
Premiums for 0.2 percent material were quoted at quotes fob hi flat/+$1.50 a tonne.
Traders said the arbitrage door to the Far East was only open for very large cargoes and as yet had done little to mop up excess Russian material.
Traders the movement of low sulphur material north had tightened the EN590 market slightly, but there was not much local demand, so the market was basically pretty balanced.
EN590 was quoted at quotes fob high +$1.50/+$3.0 a tonne, although nothing was reported to have traded.
Fuel markets were marginally better supplied after Turkey cancelled its buy tender and a trader bought high sulphur M-100 straight-run out of tankage.
The material was believed bought for high cif quotes minus $8.50 basis Algeciras.
Other material not expected to be shown to the market was suddenly offered, including Turkish straight-run and Italian high sulphur cracked.
But the new material could not completely counteract the effect of a thin Russian Black Sea schedule next week.
Demand was eased slightly by a trader covering his Spanish bunker short with Baltic Sea Russian cracked fuel.
